targetText: the Social-Democrat’s ideal should not be the trade union secretary, but the tribune of the people, who is able to react to every manifestation of tyranny and oppression, no matter where it appears, no matter what stratum or class of the people it affects
summary: An effective political leader must expose all forms of injustice in society (police brutality, government corruption, discrimination) rather than limiting themselves to narrow workplace pay disputes.
context: Lenin defines the 'tribune of the people' as a leader who connects disparate social struggles into a unified movement against the ruling regime.

targetText: To bring political knowledge to the workers the Social Democrats must go among all classes of the population; they must dispatch units of their army in all directions.
summary: Socialists must carry political agitation to every class and not confine themselves to economic disputes at the factory.
explanation: Lenin rejects the idea that workers learn politics only from their own employers. Class political consciousness comes from knowing the relations between all classes and the state, so the party must send its forces among every social stratum.
context: This passage underlies the concept of the party as a 'tribune of the people' rather than a trade union secretary.
